steps.title: Open the dashboard
steps.narration: Trendora opens on a live dashboard for the tracked stock universe, with one simple trust signal confirming today's numbers are current before you look at anything else.
steps.point_out: The green "GO — today's board is current" banner sitting right below the header.

steps.title: Browse the stock leaderboard
steps.narration: Every tracked stock gets a Leadership, Entry Quality, and Risk score — and every single one of those scores is honestly labeled with its evidence status.
steps.point_out: The "541 / 541" coverage count at the top, and a small badge next to every score in the table.

steps.title: Drill into one stock's evidence
steps.narration: Opening any stock shows its full score breakdown — and each score carries the same honest badge, so nothing is ever quietly dressed up as proven.
steps.point_out: The "Not yet proven" badge sitting next to each of AAPL's three scores.

steps.title: See the honesty hold even on a strong score
steps.narration: MU's Leadership score is strong enough to earn a C grade, but it still gets exactly the same honest badge as every other stock — strength alone never buys a free pass.
steps.point_out: MU's 77.18 Leadership score sitting right next to its "Not yet proven" badge.

steps.title: See three decades of price history
steps.narration: Stock pages default to a stock's full price history — for a long-tenured name like NVDA, that stretches all the way back to its real 1999 listing.
steps.point_out: The full-history chart running to 3025 bars, and the "Technology" sector tag above it.

steps.title: See an honestly short history for a recent listing
steps.narration: Switching to a stock that only went public a couple of years ago, like ARM, shows a much shorter chart — real and short, never stretched or invented.
steps.point_out: ARM's chart starting at its actual 2023 IPO date, with 701 bars instead of thousands.

steps.title: Audit the evidence ledger
steps.narration: The Evidence ledger is where every tested idea gets judged out loud — wins and losses both, with nothing held back.
steps.point_out: Each claim card's real out-of-sample result, like "FAIL · holdout edge -0.03%", alongside its comparison against the S&P 500 and its registration date.

steps.title: Trace evidence back to where it lives
steps.narration: Every claim on the ledger links straight back to the exact place in the product it backs, so the trail from claim to feature never dead-ends.
steps.point_out: Clicking "Backs: Stocks leaderboard" jumps straight to the leaderboard page.

steps.title: See evidence tied to today's market regime
steps.narration: Some ideas are only meaningful in a specific kind of market — this claim shows exactly how a Risk-on-only setup performed, honestly, out of sample.
steps.point_out: The "Regime: Risk-on" condition tag on its own claim card.

expect.text: Out-of-sample edge in the Risk-on regime

steps.title: See evidence tested at a longer hold
steps.narration: The same kind of idea is also retested holding for 60 days instead of the usual 20, and reports its honest result either way.
steps.point_out: The 60-day-hold claim card reading "FAIL · holdout edge -1.64%."

steps.title: See combined-factor evidence
steps.narration: Ideas that blend more than one signal — like relative strength crossed with closeness to a high — go through the exact same rigorous, out-of-sample test as any single factor.
steps.point_out: The composite claim card labeled "rs_spy_3m × high_proximity — composite."

steps.title: Re-certify factors on the full history
steps.narration: The Factor Lab confirms every tested signal has been re-checked against the platform's full three-decade history, not just a shorter recent window.
steps.point_out: The "~30 years of history" note near the top of the page.

steps.title: Open a factor's full decile breakdown
steps.narration: Clicking into a factor opens its complete decile grid, showing exactly how each tier of stocks actually performed afterward — no summary hiding the real spread.
steps.point_out: The "Decile grid — forward return" table, ranked from weakest to strongest tier.

steps.title: Check the statistical budget before it's spent
steps.narration: Trendora keeps a running account of its own statistical testing budget, so nobody can quietly run endless tests until one passes by chance.
steps.point_out: The note confirming the next canonical trial will be test #8, alongside the bar it has to clear.

steps.title: Browse the pre-registration registry
steps.narration: Every idea gets logged here — reasoning, tags, and a registration date — before it's ever tested, so nothing can be cherry-picked after the fact.
steps.point_out: Selector chips like "factor=vcp_contraction" next to each registered idea's plain-language rationale.

steps.title: Browse the graveyard of rejected ideas
steps.narration: Ideas that failed testing aren't hidden away — they're archived here in the open, so nobody wastes time re-deriving a dead idea from scratch.
steps.point_out: The full list of past rejected ideas, each with its own honest reason.

steps.title: Trace a rejected idea back to its registration
steps.narration: Clicking a rejected idea's lineage link jumps straight to its original registration row, so the whole history of an idea is always one click away.
steps.point_out: The registry page scrolling itself right to the matching row.

steps.title: Check the tester's own calibration
steps.narration: Trendora even audits its own statistical tester — running null trials and a deliberately corrupted factor to confirm the testing process itself can be trusted.
steps.point_out: The false-pass rate measured across 200 null trials, and the corrupted factor correctly labeled "expected: rejected."

steps.title: See the tracked universe in the Data Manager
steps.narration: The Data Manager shows exactly how many stocks are tracked and how complete their data is — with two separate, clearly-labeled signals instead of one confusing color.
steps.point_out: The "590 symbols" count, and a legend explaining the cell fill versus the ring around each cell.

steps.title: See the universe change over time
steps.narration: The tracked universe isn't a fixed list frozen in time — it grows and shrinks as real companies list, delist, and merge, and this page shows exactly when.
steps.point_out: The dynamic-universe membership timeline.

steps.title: See where the benchmark data comes from
steps.narration: Every index and macro series behind the scenes — the S&P 500, VIX, and more — is labeled with its real data source and how far back it goes.
steps.point_out: The provenance table listing each index's vendor and earliest available date.

steps.title: Watch for silent data drift
steps.narration: The Data Manager quietly compares freshly-pulled prices against the trusted saved history, and flags anything that was silently revised.
steps.point_out: The Live-vs-seed drift panel.

steps.title: Run an honest backfill
steps.narration: Kicking off a backfill completes cleanly and reports exactly what it did — no silent partial job, no guessed numbers.
steps.point_out: The "Snapshots backfilled" confirmation once the job finishes.

steps.title: Open the Watchlist's Concentration X-ray
steps.narration: Below the familiar saved-stocks table, the Watchlist shows exactly how concentrated those picks really are — as one clear number, not a guess.
steps.point_out: The "≈ 2.0 effective independent bets" headline, with the exact 126-trading-day window stated right next to it.

steps.title: See the real computed correlation
steps.narration: Behind that headline sits a real, computed correlation between every pair of saved stocks — not a color with nothing backing it.
steps.point_out: The ABBV × MSFT cell reading "-0.11" right where the two rows and columns cross.

steps.title: See where the watchlist is concentrated
steps.narration: Sector, theme, and shared-setup breakdowns show exactly where a watchlist leans too heavily on one thing — including an honest "Unassigned" bucket rather than a blank or crashed row.
steps.point_out: The "Technology" and "Unassigned" sector bars, plus the concentration bars beneath them.

steps.title: Check the methodology behind the headline
steps.narration: A small info icon next to the headline opens a plain-language explanation of exactly how that number gets worked out.
steps.point_out: The tooltip explaining the eigenvalues of the correlation matrix, in plain language.

expect.text: eigenvalues of the pairwise correlation matrix
